content.value_statement: DevFlow projects need consistent file names, directories, and metadata. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code shared standards for requirements and bug workflows.
actual_capabilities: Defines requirement ID and task ID formats for CC-DevFlow work.
Documents the expected folder structure for requirement and bug workflows.
Lists required YAML frontmatter fields for PRD, design, epic, and task documents.
Describes status file fields and allowed status values for workflow tracking.
Provides naming patterns for Markdown documents, scripts, directories, and contract files.
limitations: Does not validate files or run checks by itself.
Does not define agent-specific writing rules or planning methods.
Does not include complete templates for generated documents.
Applies to CC-DevFlow conventions and may not fit unrelated workflows.

use_cases.title: Align Flow Commands
use_cases.description: Use shared paths, identifiers, and status names when creating or updating DevFlow commands.

use_cases.title: Guide Agent Outputs
use_cases.description: Keep generated PRD, design, epic, and task files consistent across multiple agents.

use_cases.title: Review Project Structure
use_cases.description: Check whether a requirement or bug workspace follows the expected DevFlow layout.

prompt_templates.title: Find the Right Location
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to tell me where a DevFlow PRD file should be placed for requirement REQ-123.

prompt_templates.title: Check Naming Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these DevFlow file and directory names against the skill standards, then list any corrections.

prompt_templates.title: Review Frontmatter
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my PRD, TECH_DESIGN, EPIC, and TASKS frontmatter fields with the required DevFlow standards.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Workflow Tree
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across a full requirement workspace.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this DevFlow requirement workspace for naming, directory structure, frontmatter, status fields, and special file handling.

output_examples.input: Where should the PRD for REQ-042 be stored?
output_examples.output: The response identifies the requirement folder and states that the PRD belongs with the other REQ-042 workflow documents.

output_examples.input: Review my task IDs and labels for a DevFlow task list.
output_examples.output: The response confirms valid task ID formatting, explains parallel labels, and flags labels that do not match the standard.

output_examples.input: Check whether my workflow status fields are complete.
output_examples.output: The response lists missing tracking fields, verifies the workflow phase, and notes any status value that is not allowed.

best_practices: Use one requirement ID consistently across paths, branch names, status files, and documents.
Keep generated workflow files in the documented requirement or bug folder structure.
Check frontmatter before handoff so downstream agents can parse status and metadata.
anti_patterns: Mixing requirement IDs from different workspaces in one file tree.
Adding agent-specific writing rules to this shared file standards reference.
Committing environment files, secrets folders, or dependency folders inside DevFlow workspaces.

faq.question: Does this skill create DevFlow files?
faq.answer: No. It documents naming, structure, and metadata standards for files created by other commands and agents.

faq.question: Can it validate my repository automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can guide a review, but separate scripts or tools must perform automated validation.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What workflows does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers CC-DevFlow requirement workflows, bug workflows, status files, document metadata, and shared file naming.

faq.question: Does it include full document templates?
faq.answer: No. It references template locations and lists shared fields, but it does not include complete template contents.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: The skill says environment files and secrets folders should not be committed inside DevFlow requirement folders.
